errata.notes:
The YANG module ietf-ospf-anycast-flag@2026-05-19 in Section 4.2 contains two XPath defects that cause standards-compliant YANG 1.1 validators (RFC 7950) to reject valid OSPFv2 configurations:

1. In the augment's "when" statement:
   (a) Per RFC 9129, identity "ospf:ospfv2" (base "ospf:ospf-protocol") has no derived identities in standard OSPF configurations where rt:type is set to "ietf-ospf:ospfv2". Per RFC 7950 Section 10.4.1, derived-from() returns true only if the first argument is strictly derived from (and NOT equal to) the second argument, so derived-from(..., 'ospf:ospfv2') evaluates to false for rt:type = 'ietf-ospf:ospfv2' and makes anycast-flag invalid to configure. RFC 9129 itself uses derived-from-or-self(..., 'ospf:ospfv2').
   (b) The absolute path /rt:routing/rt:control-plane-protocols/rt:control-plane-protocol/rt:type has no predicate binding it to the enclosing control-plane-protocol instance; relative path ../../../../../rt:type scopes the check to the augmented protocol instance (from ospf:interface -> ospf:interfaces -> ospf:area -> ospf:areas -> ospf:ospf -> rt:control-plane-protocol).

2. In leaf anycast-flag's "must" statement:
   The second operand (/rt:routing/rt:control-plane-protocols/rt:control-plane-protocol/ospf:ospf/ospf:areas/ospf:area/ospf:interfaces/ospf:interface/ospf:node-flag = 'true') is an unbound absolute XPath across all OSPF interfaces on the router. Because XPath "=" over a node-set is existential, setting node-flag = 'true' on any single interface (e.g., loopback lo0) causes configuring anycast-flag = 'true' on a different interface (e.g., anycast loopback lo1) to fail validation. Per Section 2 ("Both the AC-Flag and the N-Flag MUST NOT be set to 1 for the same prefix"), the constraint applies to the same interface (../ospf:node-flag = 'true').
